sources.title: Marine Personnel Regulations, SOR/2007-115 (consolidated XML): ss. 110(2), 115, 134 (item 2(i)), Schedules 3 to 5 to Part 1, and Part 3 Division 7 (ss. 339-340, log books)
sources.publisher: Department of Justice Canada (laws-lois-xml open data repository)
sources.edition: Consolidated XML, main branch as fetched 2026-11-16
sources.notes: Read word for word from the XML. Supports: s. 110(2) documents to the examiner at least two weeks before the first exam (discharge books, certificates of discharge, testimonials with the required signatures and at least the Schedule 4 or 5 information); s. 115 the 8-hour day, 12-hour cap and divide-by-30 rules; s. 134 as an example of a certificate needing a steering testimonial; Schedule 3 (steering testimonial items and the master's declaration of hours at the wheel); Schedule 4 (deck testimonial items 1 to 12); Schedule 5 (engine testimonial, signatures of chief engineer and master or authorized representative); s. 339 (which vessels keep an official log book, united with or distinct from the deck log, timing and dating of entries, signatures); s. 340 (entries, and keeping the completed book until the earlier of five years or a change of registration). Not the official version.

sources.title: Canada Shipping Act, 2001, S.C. 2001, c. 26 (consolidated XML): ss. 23, 91-93
sources.publisher: Department of Justice Canada (laws-lois-xml open data repository)
sources.edition: Consolidated XML, main branch as fetched 2026-11-16
sources.notes: Read word for word from the XML. Supports: s. 23(a) and (b) (no wilful destruction of a required document; no false log book entry with intent to mislead and no wilful omission); s. 91 articles of agreement; s. 92 certificate of discharge provided by the authorized representative; s. 93 record of sea service kept by both the authorized representative and the crew member, in the form and for the period the Minister specifies. The Minister's specified forms and periods were not read. Not the official version.

sources.title: Navigation Safety Regulations, 2020, SOR/2020-216 (consolidated XML): ss. 136(4), 137(1), 246, 247
sources.publisher: Department of Justice Canada (laws-lois-xml open data repository)
sources.edition: Consolidated XML, main branch as fetched 2026-11-16
sources.notes: Read word for word from the XML. Supports: s. 136(4) steering gear checks, tests and emergency steering drills recorded in the official log book, or in any log book where MPR Part 3 Division 7 does not apply; s. 137(1) working language recorded the same way; s. 246 time in voice communications (UTC on an international voyage, local time otherwise, 24-hour system in four figures with the time zone identifier); s. 247 the radio record (contents, initials on each entry, kept at least 12 months after the last entry). Which vessels these sections apply to was not re-studied for this batch. Not the official version.

sources.title: Radio Aids to Marine Navigation 2026, Part 3: Vessel Traffic Services (sections 3.2 to 3.5, Tables 3-1 to 3-3, Victoria VTS Zone)
sources.publisher: Canadian Coast Guard, Government of Canada
sources.notes: Read through a fetch tool that returned the first part of the page as text, not by a person reading the page or the PDF. Text returned covered: section 3.2 (listening watch on the sector frequency, calls on sector frequencies not over one minute, loss of communication, equipment failure), the 24-hour time statement, sections 3.5.1 to 3.5.2.6 (application and the designators for each Western zone report), Table 3-1 (Victoria sector limits), Table 3-2 (Victoria sector channels: 1 = Ch 11 with Seattle Traffic on 05A for calling-in points 1, 3, 5 and 8; 2 = Ch 74; 3 = Ch 12; 4 = Ch 71; sectors 1 to 3 radar and AIS, sector 4 AIS) and Table 3-3 calling-in points 1 to 34. The Prince Rupert tables were NOT returned and are not relied on. The meaning given to each report letter (A identity, B time, C or D position, I destination and ETA, K exit, L route, N next report, P cargo, Q defects, R pollution) is a summary and must be checked against the template in section 3.4. Channels and calling-in points change: verify against the published RAMN before use.
